name: devops-ansible
description: Use when writing, reviewing, testing or running Ansible - choosing ansible-core and community package versions (control node and managed node Python), static and dynamic inventory with group_vars/host_vars, variable precedence, playbooks, roles and collections (ansible-galaxy, requirements.yml, FQCN), idempotency (changed_when/failed_when), handlers, tags, Jinja2 templates, Ansible Vault and no_log, privilege escalation, check mode and diff mode, --limit, serial/rolling updates and max_fail_percentage, block/rescue/always, performance (forks, pipelining, fact caching, strategy), ansible-lint, Molecule, execution environments (ansible-navigator, ansible-builder), project layout, and Ansible versus Terraform/OpenTofu. Not for Terraform/OpenTofu state and modules (devops-iac), Linux host internals (devops-linux), CI pipeline authoring (devops-cicd), secret stores (devops-secrets), Proxmox or OpenStack platform internals (devops-proxmox, devops-openstack) or a security hardening audit (fuse-security:security-expert).

findings.excerpt: ansible --version; ansible-galaxy collection list                 # versions first
python3 -m pip install --user ansible            # full package (inside a venv in practice)
python3 -m pip install --user ansible-core       # minimal; then ansible-galaxy collection install -r ...
pipx install --include-deps ansible              # when the OS blocks pip
